title: Hydrogen adsorption on graphene sheets and nonporous graphitized thermal carbon black at low surface coverage
material_description: GS | graphene sheets prepared from thermally expanded r-GO (GO synthesized by modified Hummers method, ref. [16]); pocket-like wrinkled-paper morphology (SEM); EDS (Table 1): C 78.88, O 13.62, P 3.24, Cl 0.12, Nb 4.14 at%
source_location: main-4.png (p. 18468), Fig. 4a, series GS@77K (filled squares), marker 1 of 12 in order of pressure
notes: archive: HYC-0135_fig4a_GS_77K.json; digitized: 0.132632 kPa, 0.0257528 mmol g-1 (pixel 209.00, 1409.50). Low-pressure cluster: markers lie close together (GS: touching squares; BP280: next to the open-star cluster and the lines), separated by 3x3 binary erosion of the page image before digitization. Units printed on Fig. 4 axes: P/kPa (pressure_bar = kPa x 0.01) and n_exc/mmol g-1; uptake_wt_pct is W1 = 0.201588 x mmol g-1 computed from the digitized value. Temperature from the legend (77 K and 87 K are printed; text: measured in baths of liquid nitrogen and liquid argon). Text: "the mean values of experimental data measured three times were used" - no individual runs or uncertainty shown, so replicates_reported = false. Degassing printed as "within vacuum at 363.15 K for 3 h and then 423.15 K for 12 h", then degassed to ultra-high vacuum at ambient temperature in the 3Flex; recorded the final step (423.15 K = 150 C, 12 h); no end pressure stated. Instrument: Micromeritics 3Flex (volumetric). Gases (hydrogen, argon, helium) "ultra-high-purity grade" (no number). Helium is listed among the gases used but the paper does not say how the free volume was determined, so calibration_described = false. Surface area/pore volumes from Table 2; the paper does not name the gas for the BET area explicitly, but its only physisorption characterization is Ar at 87 K (Fig. 2), from which PSD and pore volumes were determined by DFT (Fig. 3, Table 2); BET relative-pressure range not stated. Sample mass printed as 0.1676 g. Material class: rGO-derived graphene sheets; synthesis route recorded as the thermal expansion (reduction) of r-GO. EDS shows Nb 4.14 at% and P 3.24 at%, Cl 0.12 at%; the conclusions attribute uncertainty to "the impurity of contained within the tested GS sample"; Nb recorded as residual (unintended) metal, wt% not given (only at%); no phase identified, so not coded composite; heteroatoms not described as deliberate doping.
basis_evidence: "As per Gibbs's definition of the adsorption, the excess adsorption amount n_exc can be correlated with absolute adsorption amount n_abs as [29] n_exc = n_abs - v_a*rho_b = v_a(rho_a - rho_b). (1) where v_a is the specific volume of adsorbed phase; rho_b the density of bulk gas phase; rho_a the density of adsorbed phase." (p. 18467-18468); Fig. 4 caption: "Isotherms of excess amount of hydrogen on the GS (a) and carbon black BP280 (b)."; Fig. 4 y-axis "n_exc/mmol g-1"

source_location: main-4.png (p. 18468), Fig. 4a, series GS@77K (filled squares), marker 11 of 12 in order of pressure
notes: archive: HYC-0135_fig4a_GS_77K.json; digitized: 0.897544 kPa, 0.0947865 mmol g-1 (pixel 481.50, 1217.50). Units printed on Fig. 4 axes: P/kPa (pressure_bar = kPa x 0.01) and n_exc/mmol g-1; uptake_wt_pct is W1 = 0.201588 x mmol g-1 computed from the digitized value. Temperature from the legend (77 K and 87 K are printed; text: measured in baths of liquid nitrogen and liquid argon). Text: "the mean values of experimental data measured three times were used" - no individual runs or uncertainty shown, so replicates_reported = false. Degassing printed as "within vacuum at 363.15 K for 3 h and then 423.15 K for 12 h", then degassed to ultra-high vacuum at ambient temperature in the 3Flex; recorded the final step (423.15 K = 150 C, 12 h); no end pressure stated. Instrument: Micromeritics 3Flex (volumetric). Gases (hydrogen, argon, helium) "ultra-high-purity grade" (no number). Helium is listed among the gases used but the paper does not say how the free volume was determined, so calibration_described = false. Surface area/pore volumes from Table 2; the paper does not name the gas for the BET area explicitly, but its only physisorption characterization is Ar at 87 K (Fig. 2), from which PSD and pore volumes were determined by DFT (Fig. 3, Table 2); BET relative-pressure range not stated. Sample mass printed as 0.1676 g. Material class: rGO-derived graphene sheets; synthesis route recorded as the thermal expansion (reduction) of r-GO. EDS shows Nb 4.14 at% and P 3.24 at%, Cl 0.12 at%; the conclusions attribute uncertainty to "the impurity of contained within the tested GS sample"; Nb recorded as residual (unintended) metal, wt% not given (only at%); no phase identified, so not coded composite; heteroatoms not described as deliberate doping.
basis_evidence: "As per Gibbs's definition of the adsorption, the excess adsorption amount n_exc can be correlated with absolute adsorption amount n_abs as [29] n_exc = n_abs - v_a*rho_b = v_a(rho_a - rho_b). (1) where v_a is the specific volume of adsorbed phase; rho_b the density of bulk gas phase; rho_a the density of adsorbed phase." (p. 18467-18468); Fig. 4 caption: "Isotherms of excess amount of hydrogen on the GS (a) and carbon black BP280 (b)."; Fig. 4 y-axis "n_exc/mmol g-1"
